```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Each fit takes several minutes on 16 cores (97,806 occasions), so the
# results were saved by dev/precompute-markov.R and are read from
# markov-results.rds.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 4, out.width = "100%")
library(crywolf)
res <- readRDS("markov-results.rds")
row <- function(model, var) {
  t <- res$summary[[model]]
  t[t$variable == var, ]
}
ci <- function(model, var, digits = 2) {
  r <- row(model, var)
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f (%.", digits, "f to %.", digits, "f)"),
          r$mean, r$lower, r$upper)
}
```

```{r stale, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat(crywolf:::.stale_note(res, "markov-results.rds"))
```

The occupancy model treats the occasions of a site as independent given
whether the site is occupied. With short occasions this is often false. A
Common Pauraque that starts calling at dusk is recorded in several
consecutive recordings, then falls silent for a while: detections come in
runs. Independent occasions spread the detections of an occupied site more
evenly than that, so the model underestimates how often an occupied site
yields no detection at all on a given night, and overstates how much
information each detection carries.

`fp_occu(markov = )` adds a first-order Markov term for true detections.
This article fits it to the `curiango` data (Piatti et al., 2026) and
compares it with the model of independent occasions.

## The model

With `markov = "time"`, the probability that occasion $k$ of an occupied
site $i$ is a detection depends on whether occasion $k - 1$ was:

$$
\mathrm{logit}(p_{11,ik}) = \mathbf{z}_{ik}^\top \boldsymbol{\alpha} + \theta\, y_{i,k-1},
$$

where $\mathbf{z}_{ik}$ are the detection covariates with coefficients
$\boldsymbol{\alpha}$, $y_{i,k-1}$ is the observed automated detection on the
previous occasion, and $\theta$ (reported as `det_y_prev`) is the change in
the logit of detection right after a detection. A positive $\theta$ means
runs. The prior on $\theta$ is the slope prior of `fp_priors()`, Normal(0,
2.5) by default.

Three details matter.

* The term acts on the occupied state only. False positives stay
  independent among occasions, since a classifier's errors are not expected
  to come in runs in the same way.
* The previous occasion must be one time step earlier, where the step is
  the shortest interval between consecutive occasions of a site. The first
  occasion of each site, and an occasion that follows a gap, has
  $y_{i,k-1} = 0$; a run is never carried across a missing recording.
* The previous detection is taken from the data, so posterior predictive
  checks (`fp_ppc()`) replicate each occasion given the observed previous
  one, while `simulate()` generates whole runs in order.

## Fitting

```{r fit, eval = FALSE}
zs <- function(v) as.numeric(scale(v))
m <- curiango$minutes
auto <- data.frame(site_night = m$site_night, time = m$time,
                   y = as.integer(m$conf_custom >= 0.40),
                   bio = zs(m$bio), aci = zs(m$aci), recorder = m$site)
nt <- curiango$nights
sites <- data.frame(site_night = nt$site_night, temp = zs(nt$temp),
                    rh = zs(nt$rh), moon = zs(log(nt$moon)))
ver <- data.frame(site_night = curiango$verified$site_night,
                  y = curiango$verified$y)
d <- fp_data(auto, sites, ver, site = "site_night", recorder = "recorder")

m0 <- fp_occu(d, occ = ~ temp + rh + moon, det = ~ bio + aci, fp = ~ 1,
              threads_per_chain = 4)
m1 <- fp_occu(d, occ = ~ temp + rh + moon, det = ~ bio + aci, fp = ~ 1,
              markov = "time", threads_per_chain = 4)
```

The recordings were made every 15 minutes, so the time step is 15 minutes.
Of the `r format(res$n_occasions, big.mark = ",")` occasions,
`r format(res$n_gaps, big.mark = ",")` follow a longer interval within the
same night and start a new run. Each fit took about
`r round(mean(res$minutes))` minutes with four chains of four threads.

## Results

Both fits converged: the largest R-hat was
`r sprintf("%.3f", res$diagnostics$independent$max_rhat)` and
`r sprintf("%.3f", res$diagnostics$markov$max_rhat)`, the smallest bulk
effective sample size `r round(res$diagnostics$independent$min_ess_bulk)` and
`r round(res$diagnostics$markov$min_ess_bulk)`, with
`r res$diagnostics$independent$divergences` and
`r res$diagnostics$markov$divergences` divergent transitions.

The run effect is large: $\theta$ = `r ci("markov", "det_y_prev")` on the
logit scale. Right after a detection, the odds of another detection in the
next recording are about
`r sprintf("%.1f", exp(row("markov", "det_y_prev")$mean))` times as high as after a recording without one.

```{r estimates}
vars <- c("occ_temp", "occ_rh", "occ_moon", "det_(Intercept)", "det_y_prev",
          "p10_ref")
est <- purrr::imap(res$summary, function(t, nm) {
  t <- t[t$variable %in% vars, c("variable", "mean", "lower", "upper")]
  data.frame(model = nm, t)
}) |> purrr::list_rbind()
est[c("mean", "lower", "upper")] <- signif(est[c("mean", "lower", "upper")], 3)
est
```

The occupancy effects barely move: temperature
`r ci("independent", "occ_temp")` without the term and
`r ci("markov", "occ_temp")` with it, relative humidity
`r ci("independent", "occ_rh")` and `r ci("markov", "occ_rh")`. The
false-positive rate at the reference values falls from
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * row("independent", "p10_ref")$mean)` to
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * row("markov", "p10_ref")$mean)`: without the
term, part of the clustering of detections is attributed to false
positives.

### Does the model reproduce the runs?

Data simulated from each fit (50 datasets, parameters drawn from the
posterior) can be compared with the observed lengths of runs of consecutive
detections:

```{r runs, fig.cap = "Number of runs of consecutive detections of each length in the observed data (black) and in 50 datasets simulated from each fit (mean and 95% range)."}
lev <- names(res$runs_observed)
sims <- purrr::imap(res$runs_simulated, function(mat, nm) {
  data.frame(model = nm, length = factor(lev, levels = lev),
             mean = colMeans(mat),
             lower = purrr::map_dbl(seq_along(lev), function(j) stats::quantile(mat[, j], 0.025)),
             upper = purrr::map_dbl(seq_along(lev), function(j) stats::quantile(mat[, j], 0.975)))
}) |> purrr::list_rbind()
obs <- data.frame(length = factor(lev, levels = lev),
                  count = as.numeric(res$runs_observed))
ggplot2::ggplot(sims, ggplot2::aes(length, mean, colour = model)) +
  ggplot2::geom_pointrange(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                           position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.4)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = obs, ggplot2::aes(length, count), colour = "black",
                      shape = 4, size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(independent = "#FF3EA5", markov = "#2DE2E6")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Run length (recordings)", y = "Number of runs", colour = "Model") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

```{r runs-table, echo = FALSE}
tab <- rbind(observed = as.numeric(res$runs_observed),
             independent = round(colMeans(res$runs_simulated$independent)),
             markov = round(colMeans(res$runs_simulated$markov)))
colnames(tab) <- lev
tab
```

Independent occasions produce too many isolated detections and far too few
long runs: `r round(mean(res$runs_simulated$independent[, 5]))` runs of five
or more recordings on average, against
`r as.numeric(res$runs_observed[5])` observed. With the Markov term the
simulated counts are close to the observed ones at every length.

### Posterior predictive check and LOO

The Freeman-Tukey discrepancy of `fp_ppc()` sums, over sites, how far the
detections of each site are from what the model expects:

```{r ppc}
data.frame(model = names(res$ppc),
           p_value = purrr::map_dbl(res$ppc, "p_value"),
           observed = round(purrr::map_dbl(res$ppc, function(p) mean(p$fit_obs))),
           replicated = round(purrr::map_dbl(res$ppc, function(p) mean(p$fit_rep))))
```

The Markov term brings the observed discrepancy closer to the replicated
one, but both p-values are
`r paste(unique(purrr::map_dbl(res$ppc, "p_value")), collapse = " and ")`: the detections of some site-nights remain
further from their expected values than the model allows. The discrepancy
is computed per site-night, so it does not measure runs directly, and the
remaining misfit may come from variation among nights that the covariates
do not explain. `vignette("site_effects")` adds a site effect on true
detection to these fits; leave-one-site-out comparison prefers the model
with both terms.

Leave-one-site-out cross-validation prefers the Markov model, by
`r round(-res$loo$elpd_diff[2])` units of expected log predictive density,
`r round(-res$loo$elpd_diff[2] / res$loo$se_diff[2])` times its standard
error:

```{r loo}
res$loo[, c("model", "elpd_diff", "se_diff")]
```

## When to use it

* With occasions of a few minutes and a species that calls in bouts, try
  the Markov term and compare with LOO and a posterior predictive check.
* With one occasion per night or per visit, runs are rare and the term adds
  little.
* The term needs the time of each occasion. Record it, and check how many
  occasions follow gaps, since each gap restarts a run.

## References

Piatti, L., de Sousa, D. L. H., Oliveira, B. S., de Melo, A. V., Sugai,
L. S. M., & Provete, D. B. (2026). Methodological choices influence
ecological inference in passive acoustic monitoring of a Neotropical
nightjar. *Journal of Avian Biology*, in press.
